title: Travel File Call
warm:
Pell's travel file aged wrong on speakerphone in Nolan Greer's study while [player_name] watched cufflinks click through every soft synonym for gone. "She's traveling," Marcus Pell repeated, and the itinerary dates had the polished emptiness of stories that had outlived their usefulness. Crownspire night pressed the glass. Detective Imani Brooks's interest was escalating toward homicide language downstairs; Vivienne's unused perfume still haunted the bath; no body map appeared in any PDF Pell could email.

"Zurich last month," Pell said. "Milan before that. Private desk confirms departure holds. What it does not confirm is presence at either end in a way that would satisfy a detective who has stopped smiling in lobbies."

[player_name]—early thirties, across the hall, soft alibi listening like a second counsel—felt weekly-to-monthly-to-gone rearrange itself behind her teeth. "So traveling is still not a corpse and still not a return. Willing, paid, dead, staging—all still fit inside those holds. You are selling us a fog with letterhead."

Nolan's mouth was a hard line. Brutal charm spent. "Brooks will call fog obstruction soon. Soft interview windows shrink when travel ages past courtesy."

Elevator chime. Wine ring on the study's side table from an hour that had pretended to be ordinary. Rhea Quinn's slate downstairs still held blank marks Brooks wanted to photograph. Black-car nights hummed in [player_name]'s memory without becoming a settled fate.

"You have two useful next moves," Pell continued, mild as poison. "Follow the hangar lead alone if you insist on eyes without my paperwork—perfume, bags, whatever romantic evidence you think will clarify absence without clarifying guilt. Or return [player_name] to Brooks's soft interview door and let Nolan move to relieve the pressure while I keep the travel file from becoming a homicide exhibit."

Nolan looked at [player_name] as if the choice were a kiss he could not finish for her. "Alone at the hangar means you see what Pell will not put on letterhead. Soft interview door means you watch me try to buy you air while Brooks tilts colder. Neither writes Vivienne's ending. Both spend the hour this call just ruined."

[player_name] tasted wrong itineraries and unfinished want. Travel had always been the softest lie Crownspire sold. Tonight it aged like wine left open—still liquid, no longer kind.

[player_name] walked once around the study while Pell kept talking letterhead fog. Locked drawer. Window glass. Nolan's wrist telling lies in metal. Soft alibi posture was harder to hold when travel dates looked like absences wearing stamps. Brooks's colder questions lived in the room like a fourth person Pell refused to name.

"Relief at the interview door is not absolution," she told Nolan when Pell muted. "It is theater. Hangar alone is not justice. It is touching what theater leaves out. I need you to stop looking at me like both options are ways to keep me soft."

"They are ways to keep you alive in the file," Nolan said. "Soft is the side effect. Or the point. I stopped being able to tell the difference the night the slate went blank and you still answered my knock."

Crownspire's hush scored the choice. Soft alibi was never pink; soft meant pliable evidence—the mistress money preferred when a wife thinned to silence. [player_name] refused to become only that preference even while her body still answered Nolan's door. Brooks's escalating file, Rhea's eyes, Pell's letterhead, Vivienne's open fates: every pressure asked for a verb. She would give one. She would not give a corpse she had not seen.

Pell unmuted to add a private-plane desk confirmation that confirmed nothing human—only holds, only fog, only the kind of presence that satisfied boards and failed detectives. [player_name] wrote none of it down; writing made soft into exhibit. Nolan watched her refuse the pen and almost smiled. Almost. Soft interview door would require her to sit under Brooks's eyes with travel-lie residue on her tongue. Hangar alone would require her to touch what letterhead refused. She thought of weekly silk crossings she had witnessed from across the hall, monthly politeness, then blank—and how every stage had still left room for hope that Vivienne was in Milan under another name. Hope was not evidence. Hope was the softest drug Crownspire sold beside wine.
hot:
Pell's travel file aged wrong in [player_name]'s ears while Nolan Greer's cufflinks clicked through every synonym for gone and her body treated the study like a bed with the lights of the law still on. "She's traveling," counsel repeated, and the emptiness in the dates made [player_name]'s nipples tighten with fury and dread braided filthy. Soft alibi heat had nowhere polite to go. Brooks tilted colder downstairs without a corpse; Vivienne's perfume ghosted the bath; mid-want kept score anyway.

"Fog with letterhead," [player_name] said, early thirties, across-the-hall, thighs tight under the desk's shadow as if posture could hide pulse. Nolan's hand found her knee under wood—claiming, warning, hungry—and she almost opened for him out of spite at Pell's mild voice.

"Hangar alone," Pell offered, "if you want perfume and bags without my paperwork. Or soft interview door—Nolan relieves pressure, I keep travel from becoming homicide exhibit."

Nolan's mouth near her temple, whisper for her only: "Alone you see what letterhead won't hold while your cunt still remembers my almost-kiss. Interview door you watch me buy you air with my hands off you in public and my want screaming private. Neither settles her. Both spend this ruined hour."

Elevator chime trembled through the floor into her bones. She chose between solitude's evidence and the soft interview's political heat, unfinished, perfume-haunted, travel-lie bitter on her tongue beside the taste of him.

Under the desk his hand had been a secret ventricle of the ruined call—thumb stroking the inside of her knee until she had to bite honesty quiet for Pell. Soft interview door would require her to sit with that throb locked down under badge light. Hangar alone would let her walk the throb into dark and invent whether evidence could substitute for his mouth. She was so tired of substitutions. Mid-want did not care. Mid-want wanted a verb with a body attached, even if the body was only her own hands shaking on a packed bag that should not still be packed.

Heat advanced trust-versus-complicity rather than decorating fear. Her body kept score—thighs, breath, unfinished mouth—while law pressure climbed. Nolan remaining the only LI meant every throb had a name and a risk. She exited mid-want on purpose, Vivienne still contested, Brooks still rising, soft alibi still wearing her pulse.

His thumb under the desk had found the tendon of her inner knee and stayed there through Pell's fog like a promise and a leash. Soft interview would demand she cross her legs over that ghost-touch while Brooks asked last-known questions. Hangar alone would let her walk until the ghost-touch became her own fingers shaking on evidence. She was furious at how erotic administrative cruelty felt in this building. Furious at how her cunt kept translating danger into want. Nolan's eyes said he knew. Cufflinks said he lied about knowing. Both tells lived between her legs.
